audience.programmeDescription: VU Public Administration and Organization Science studies how governments, businesses and civil society make decisions, organize people and implement change. The Dutch bachelor combines political and organizational analysis, law, economics, communication and social research. This comparison shows the Besturen route, its open study space and linked team-research and individual-project sequence.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified directions: public governance and policy; organizational leadership and responsible decisions; and climate science with public governance. Each has a substantial social-science response to the field, with different priorities. Leadership uses specific ethical and emotion-theory foundations; the climate direction includes substantial scientific and technical study. These do not confer the same disciplinary degree, specialist practicum, linked team-research and individual-project sequence or automatic postgraduate eligibility.

curriculum.limitation: This Dutch, full-time pathway follows Besturen (Public Governance). Year 1 contains 60 EC of common courses. Year 2 combines 48 EC of required study with two separate 6-EC restricted choices, illustrated here by Beyond Gender Inequalities and AI & Society. Year 3 contains 30 EC of open choice, a 6-EC governance course, 12 EC of team research and a 12-EC individual project. The project develops a paper and oral defence from the team-research findings. Methods courses have sequential participation requirements; the bachelor project requires 90 EC from Years 1–2 and a passed Governance or Consultancy Practicum. Mentorship and the Dutch diagnostic/remedial language requirements add no separate credits; completion conditions apply before the relevant grades are awarded. Practicals and tutorials require attendance. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to exceptions. Open choice requires approval except for specified options; it normally excludes introductory courses and must include at least 12 EC at level 300. A single 6-EC introductory prerequisite may be approved within a coherent package. Internships require prior approval, and overlapping minor content requires replacement.

componentNotes.y2-06: Selected 6-EC interdisciplinary option in the first restricted-choice slot; one of three available subjects.
componentNotes.y2-07: Selected 6-EC interdisciplinary option in the second restricted-choice slot; one of three available subjects.
componentNotes.y3-01: 30 EC of approved open choice, with applicable level and overlap requirements; no particular minor or internship is assumed.
componentNotes.y3-03: 12 EC empirical team research for an external client, with group proposal/report and individual professional-skills/reflection assessments. Entry follows participation in Quantitative Methods; weekly tutorials are mandatory.
componentNotes.y3-04: 12 EC individual academic paper and oral defense reflecting theoretically and methodologically on group-practicum findings. Requires 90 EC from Years 1–2 and passed Governance or Consultancy Practicum; Year 3 mentorship must be complete before the grade is awarded.

cellNotes.text: A partial gender-and-inclusion correspondence: UCR emphasises minority experiences, psychological safety and survey research; VU has a broader intersectional gender-studies approach.

notes.text: The VU route integrates public administration and organizational science with a dedicated methods sequence, Governance Practicum, client-based team research and an individual academic paper and defense. UCR offers substantial related disciplinary study, but does not automatically reproduce that complete professional and research sequence. Literary production, emotion theory and environmental technologies are not substitutes for it.

The climate alternative deliberately combines environmental science and technical options with social, legal, economic and governance study. Its materials, resource and energy courses supply domain knowledge rather than public-management methods. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval; it is not automatically the VU practicum or bachelor project.

selectedModalDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedModalDescriptions.description: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

selectedModalDescriptions.description: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices.

selectedModalDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedModalDescriptions.description: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
